{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"480e2fbdcdc27f36444098f9496fb24b01249192d9deaed31305c0e4d60c8c9f","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:50","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing roads with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles and large vehicles","heading":"C — Sharing roads with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles and large vehicles","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Sharing roads with pedestrians, cyclists, motorcycles and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk, stopping when required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Do not overtake a vehicle that has stopped to let a pedestrian cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Watch especially carefully for children near schools and homes, and do not speed in school zones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Check traffic carefully before getting out of a vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians must use an available sidewalk; without one, walk on the shoulder facing traffic and as far from the roadway as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
A pedestrian walking along a road at night must carry a light or reflector. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Light-colored clothing is recommended for pedestrians when possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
Walking on a highway under the influence of alcohol or narcotic drugs is prohibited. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
Do not stand on a highway to solicit a ride or conduct business. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians should cross at marked crosswalks; when none exists, cross at an intersection; without an intersection, look both ways and cross quickly when needed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians must follow WALK and DON’T WALK signals; blinking DON’T WALK prohibits beginning the crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Before crossing at an intersection, pedestrians must watch for turning cars. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
Diagonal intersection crossings are prohibited unless traffic-control signals authorize them. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians have priority at an intersection when their green light or WALK signal permits crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians have priority while crossing in either a marked or unmarked crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians on a sidewalk have priority as it crosses an alley, driveway or entrance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A01
Blind pedestrians crossing with a white cane or guide dog have priority. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians must yield when crossing outside a marked crosswalk or an unmarked intersection crosswalk. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A01
Pedestrians must yield when crossing a roadway where an overhead crossing or pedestrian tunnel is provided. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
Cyclists may use Delaware public roads except limited-access highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
When a lane is too narrow for safe side-by-side travel, a motorist passing a bicycle must change lanes, including across a double yellow line, and leave at least three feet. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
A motorist must not sound the horn at a cyclist unless danger is imminent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A02
A cyclist should keep right as far as safety permits. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A02
A bike box is a designated space at the front of an intersection traffic lane that makes cyclists visible and assists turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A02
A bike box helps prevent conflicts with right-turning vehicles and limits vehicle encroachment on the crosswalk. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A03
A two-way cycle track separates cycling from motor traffic and carries bicycles both ways along one side of the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A03
A street-level protected cycle track can use a parking lane or another barrier to separate it from motor traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A03
Passing too close at higher speeds can create air pressure capable of making a cyclist crash, especially beside a truck or bus. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A03
If a lane cannot safely fit a vehicle and bicycle together, the passing driver must move fully into another lane, even across double yellow lines. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A03
In an unusually wide lane that safely fits both, a driver may pass a bicycle within the lane only while slowing and maintaining at least three feet of clearance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A03
On a two-lane road, if sight distance or opposing traffic prevents safe bicycle passing, follow at a safe gap until passing becomes safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A03
After passing a cyclist, allow ample clearance before moving back right because the bicycle may be faster than expected. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A03
The detailed bicycle-passing rule allows horn use only to warn of an imminent collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A03
Check carefully for cyclists before entering a road or turning, and do not pass a cyclist only to turn immediately across the bicycle’s path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A04
Parents or guardians can be responsible for a child’s cycling traffic-law violations and for an under-18 child riding without a helmet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A04
Before riding in traffic, a cyclist should master straight riding, turns and smooth stops. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A04
Cyclists should be prepared to yield to motor vehicles at intersections even when they believe they have priority. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A04
At night, a bicycle requires a white headlamp and red rear reflector; extra reflectors and a red taillamp are helpful. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A04
Predictable cycling means traveling with traffic, signaling intentions early and choosing a path that avoids sudden swerves into traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F40 | anchor: A04
In an unusually wide lane, a cyclist should ride on its right side to permit safe in-lane passing when the cyclist feels safe doing so. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F41 | anchor: A04
A bicycle used at night needs a white headlight visible at 500 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F42 | anchor: A04
A bicycle used at night needs a red rear reflector visible at 600 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F43 | anchor: A04
Nighttime bicycle side visibility requires either reflective material visible from both sides at 600 feet or a lamp visible from both sides at 500 feet. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F44 | anchor: A04
A bicycle taillight is recommended. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F45 | anchor: A04
A bicycle rider must sit on or astride a permanent seat. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F46 | anchor: A04
A bicycle may carry a passenger only when designed for one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F47 | anchor: A04
A cyclist must not cling to another vehicle on the highway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F48 | anchor: A04
A cyclist must not ride facing highway traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F49 | anchor: A04
A bicycle rider must keep at least one hand on the handlebars. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F50 | anchor: A04
Cyclists must yield to pedestrians on sidewalks and crosswalks and sound an audible warning before passing them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F51 | anchor: A04
Cyclists must not use a headset that covers both ears. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-F52 | anchor: A05
Every cyclist younger than 18 must wear a correctly fitted, fastened bicycle helmet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F53 | anchor: A05
A cyclist must stop at a stop sign where the intersecting major road has at least three travel lanes. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F54 | anchor: A05
A cyclist must stop if a motor vehicle is already stopped at the stop sign the cyclist approaches. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F55 | anchor: A05
Heavy traffic requiring a stop for safety also requires a cyclist to stop at the sign. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F56 | anchor: A05
At a minor-road stop sign without a stopped vehicle ahead, a cyclist may slow, yield to vehicles at or approaching the intersection, and proceed cautiously without stopping. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F57 | anchor: A05
A shared-lane marking reminds motorists and cyclists that both may lawfully use the lane and supports safe positioning and passing. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F58 | anchor: A05
Check blind spots frequently for motorcycles, especially before intersection turns or entry from a side road or driveway. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F59 | anchor: A05
Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other highway users. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-F60 | anchor: A05
Motorcycles can be difficult to detect, and their distance and speed can be hard for drivers to judge. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0099]
